readerContract.humanQuestion: Is AI bad for the environment?
readerContract.promisedPayoff: Understand the real environmental costs, what changes their scale, and why efficiency and total demand can move in opposite directions.
readerContract.priorKnowledge: Adult beginner; no energy units or AI vocabulary assumed.
readerContract.centralMentalModel: AI needs physical computers, electricity and cooling. Electricity generation affects emissions; water and hardware add distinct impacts. Per-task efficiency can improve while total use grows faster. A particular environmental benefit needs evidence; it cannot erase all costs.
readerContract.dailyLifeConnection: Generating a short text answer and repeatedly generating video are different amounts of computing work.
readerContract.surfaceJob: A concise reviewed answer to an explicit question, with sources and correction controls.
readerContract.desiredFeeling: Informed without being shamed or falsely reassured.

draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: Yes. AI has environmental costs, including electricity, water and hardware.
causalSequence: AI needs physical computers, electricity and cooling.
Electricity generation affects emissions; water and hardware add distinct impacts.
Per-task efficiency can improve while total use grows faster.
A particular environmental benefit needs evidence; it cannot erase all costs.
draftArchitecture.workedCase: Simple text versus repeated video generation illustrates different computing demands without a universal ratio.
draftArchitecture.transferCase: A company says its AI is greener because each task uses less power: total use may still grow.
draftArchitecture.usefulAction: Recognize what an environmental claim counts: energy, local water, hardware and total demand.
draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure: Direct answer then connected paragraphs; dated source labels; no forced followup.
draftArchitecture.antiTemplateDecision: Do not repeat the old FAQ scaffold or force a pop-culture reference.

humourPlan.lessonJob: None required; precision and recognisable everyday situations provide engagement.
